correctness.rationale: Cyclic subgroups with unit first coordinate normalize to p distinct order-p^2 H_t=<1,t>; those of order p not contained in one of them are precisely p K_s=<ps,1>, making 2p maximal directions. For character (k,l), the annihilator tests are H_t iff k+p*l*t=0 mod p^2, and K_s iff k*s+l=0 mod p. The Gram of unnormalized line sums has eigenvalue sum_{annihilators}|H|, giving exactly the three stated spectral levels and multiplicities p^2(p-1),p^2-1,1. For every H_t and K_s, a frequency annihilated by no other maximal direction proves indispensable. With direction weights define u_s=p beta_s, v_t=p^2 alpha_t; the nonzero mean-zero energies are {u_s},{v_t} and sum_s u_s. Positivity implies max/min >=p with equality iff every u_s=m and each v_t in [m,pm]; this gives sqrt(p). Independently counted exact annihilators and spectra for p=2,3,5,7, including every direction exclusive witness. Counting normalization and constant frequency were checked separately.

value.rationale: The first nonhomocyclic rank-two prime-power torus is a natural minimal test of line-sum tomography beyond equal invariant factors. The full all-prime spectrum and weight equality class are exact structural information rather than incidental finite ranks.
